newsitem.title: GERMANY: Grundig sees 1997 loss, 1998 oper profit.
newsitem.headline: Grundig sees 1997 loss, 1998 oper profit.

text.p: Loss-making German consumer electronics maker Grundig AG expects to post another loss this year, but hopes to show an operating profit in early 1998, chairman Pieter van der Wal told a news conference.
The company is actively seeking new partners following the surprise pullout earlier this week of Philips N.V., which opens opportunities as well as risks, van der Wal said.
Philips retains its 32 percent stake, but will scale back its role to that of a passive minority stakeholder. It has lost 1.5 billion marks ($951 million) on its Grundig investment since 1984.
Grundig plans to shed about a third of its workforce, cutting it to about 6,000 by the end of 1997 from the current 8,500.
"There is no reason for panic," van der Wal said, adding that the company remains debt-free. Van der Wal, who took on his post less than a year ago, intends to stay.

The company will show an improved result but still be in the red this year, van der Wal said. It will be able to cover the loss from reserves. Sales will be about three billion marks ($1.9 billion). Earlier, he had estimated the 1996 loss at 250 million marks, narrowing from a record 600 million mark loss the year before.
Grundig may operate on its own for awhile, but in the long term it will need a strong partner, van der Wal said.
Grundig's search includes companies outside the audio-video sphere, and he expects to find a partner by the end of this year, he said.
Bavarian Premier Edmund Stoiber said late on Wednesday the state would not take a stake in Grundig.
Van der Wal said an over-concentration in the European and German markets, and an overly broad product palette were the main reasons for Grundig's difficulties.
Grundig will shift its television production to Austria. ($1=1.5772 Mark)
